item.title: Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.00249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we define a new partial distance on hyperspaces consisting of closed balls, which is a partial metric in the sense of Matthews. We prove that these partial metric spaces are complete if and only if the metric spaces from which the corresponding ball spaces arise are complete. Finally, we compare the topology induced by the new partial distance with that induced by the classical Hausdorff distance.
item.dc:creator: Dariusz Bugajewski, Piotr Ma\'ckowiak

item.title: Continuous, locally Lipschitz and Lipschitz selections for intuitionistic fuzzy sets, with applications to expert voting
item.description:
arXiv:2611.00857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies continuous selections in the framework of intuitionistic fuzzy sets. To each intuitionistic fuzzy set $A=(\mu,
u)$ on a topological space $X$ we associate the interval-valued map $F_{A}(x)=[\mu(x),1-
u(x)]$, whose width is the hesitation degree. Hence, in this setting, a selection of $F_{A}$ is an ordinary fuzzy membership function compatible with the intuitionistic information, and every selection is the membership function of Atanassov's operator $D_{\vartheta}$ for a suitable pointwise parameter $\vartheta$. When $X$ is normal and $\mu$, $
u$ are upper semi-continuous, a continuous selection exists by the Kat\v{e}tov--Tong insertion theorem. We show that upper semi-continuity arises naturally in a voting model, in which a panel of experts divides a metric universe into closed regions of acceptance and rejection, and for this model we construct an explicit continuous selection, the consensus selection, illustrated by a non-compact example in the plane. On metric spaces we characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets that admit an $L$-Lipschitz selection through a non-local version of the condition $\mu+
u\leq 1$, and we give the largest and the smallest such selections in closed form. Finally, we prove that the set of continuous selections depends in a $1$-Lipschitz way on the intuitionistic fuzzy set, with respect to the Hausdorff-type distance of Grzegorzewski. We also characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets admitting locally Lipschitz selections.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Failla, Gianmarco La Rosa, Marco Elio Tabacchi

item.title: Sequential convergence in the lower topology and co-sobriety of Scott spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how order structure controls sequential convergence in the lower topology of a poset and how this, in turn, governs topological duality and co-sobriety of Scott spaces. We first give a purely order-theoretic characterization of lower convergence. For complete lattices this yields a lower-limsup formula, and on complete chains the lower limsup coincides with the usual lattice limsup. We also characterize first countability of the lower topology at a point by the existence of a countable coinitial subset outside its principal ideal. We prove that every compact saturated subset of a Scott space is sequentially closed in the lower topology and deduce that, for every poset, the lower topology and the co-compact (de Groot dual) topology of its Scott space have exactly the same convergent sequences and limits. For coherent Scott spaces we identify the lower closure of a $k$-irreducible compact saturated set with its double-cone closure and obtain an infimum criterion for co-sobriety. Consequently, every bounded-complete dcpo with sequential lower topology has a co-sober Scott space. In particular, every countable bounded-complete dcpo, and hence every countable complete lattice, has a co-sober Scott space.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoquan Xu, Wei Ji

item.title: A co-sober Alexandrov space whose Scott power space is not co-sober
item.description: arXiv:2611.01516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Scott power construction does not preserve co-sobriety. For a dcpo $P$, let $\operatorname{Fin}(P)$ be the poset of nonempty finitely generated upper sets ordered by reverse inclusion. We prove that co-sobriety of $\Sigma\operatorname{Fin}(P)$ implies co-sobriety of $\Sigma P$. The proof adapts the point-saturation and union argument used for full compact saturated power posets; the finite step follows from a result of Heckmann and Keimel. Applying this transfer to a dcpo with a non-co-sober Scott space yields a co-sober Alexandrov space whose Scott power space is not co-sober. We also construct a countable example for which the Smyth power poset is countable. In the countable example, the same poset is co-sober under the upper Vietoris topology but not under the Scott topology.
item.dc:creator: Wei Ji, Xiaoquan Xu

item.title: A study for well-filtered spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we focus on well-filtered spaces. By using the Rudin sets and WD sets, we obtain the following results: (1) The product of arbitrary many Scott well-filtered dcpos is still well-filtered with respect to the Scott topology. Thus we give positive answers for two questions proposed by Xu and Zhao; (2) Let P be a dcpo with {\Sigma}K(P) being well-filtered and Q a RB-domain. Then {\Sigma}K(P\times Q) is well- filtered if K(P\times Q) is a dcpo; (3) A intrinsic characterization of the WD sets is given by using Scott open filters.
item.dc:creator: Zhengmao He

item.title: Kernel retracts of co-sober spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kernel retracts of co-sober spaces need not be co-sober, even when the ambient space is countably infinite and compact. We construct a co-sober $T_0$-space $Y$ and a continuous idempotent map $k\colon Y\to Y$ satisfying $k(y)\leq_Y y$ in the specialization order, whose image with the subspace topology is not co-sober. The construction starts from a countable compact $T_1$ KC anti-Hausdorff space of van Douwen type and adjoins an infinite chain. We classify the $k$-irreducible compact saturated subsets of the extension and show that each is a point saturation. The kernel operator collapses the added chain to a distinguished point while fixing the original space, thereby recovering the non-co-sober seed as its image. This answers negatively two questions of Xu and Zhao, concerning continuous kernel operators and arbitrary retracts, and contrasts with the known preservation of co-sobriety by continuous closure operators.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoquan Xu, Fengshuo Xu, Haitao Ji, Dong Qiu

item.title: Wilker property, function spaces and hyperspaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Wilker property requires that a compact set covered by two open sets admit compact covering pieces inside those open sets. We study this property through products, compact-open function spaces and hyperspaces. We construct countable compact Fr\'echet--Urysohn $T_1$ hereditarily Wilker spaces with non-Wilker products and squares. For spaces whose compact subsets are closed, Wilker-ness is equivalent to every compact subspace being Hausdorff; this yields a positive product theorem when one Wilker factor has closed compact subsets. For an irreducible subset system $H$, we characterize preservation of $H$-sobriety by compact-open function spaces in terms of $H$-supercompactness of compact subsets of the domain, and show that Wilker spaces satisfy this criterion. The Hoare hyperspace of a space is Wilker exactly when binary union on the Scott space of its open-set lattice is jointly continuous for the ordinary product topology. Consequently, the Hoare construction preserves and reflects Wilker-ness on consonant bases, although preservation fails in general. We also identify core-compactness of the base with local compactness of its Hoare hyperspace and prove that the Smyth construction reflects Wilker-ness.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoquan Xu

item.title: Subset-system derived topologies and coreflective categories of $T_0$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a subset system $H$ on $T_0$-spaces, we associate with each topology a closure-testing derived topology and study the fixed points of this operator. The $H$-determined topologies above a given topology are closed under intersections and hence determine a least fixed-point hull. We prove that this hull is obtained by transfinite iteration, is functorial, and defines a right adjoint to the inclusion of $H$-determined spaces into $\mathbf{Top}_0$. Consequently, the corresponding full subcategory is coreflective and complete. We isolate restriction-stability and open-locality hypotheses under which determinedness is inherited by closed and open subspaces, and we establish a general non-reflectivity criterion. If $H$ is contained in the directed-subset system, the category of $H$-determined spaces is Cartesian closed; its exponentials are obtained by coreflecting the pointwise convergence topology on continuous maps. The construction subsumes familiar monotone- and irreducible-determined cases while separating the formal consequences of the subset-system axioms from the additional hypotheses needed for heredity and exponentials. It therefore provides a uniform categorical mechanism for producing complete Cartesian closed categories of $T_0$-spaces with explicit higher-order function spaces, as required in denotational semantics.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoquan Xu, Xinjie Huang, Yi Yang

item.title: Uniformization of topological MV-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.01779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every topological MV-algebra the topology is induced by a uniformity. As a application, we obtain that every topological MV-algebra is completely regular and every \(T_0\) first countable topological MV-algebra is metrizable.
item.dc:creator: Li-Hong Xie, Jiang Yang

item.title: Uniform retractions onto a probability measure algebra and an application to topological groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.01802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the indicator functions form a uniformly continuous retract of the set of $[0,1]$-valued functions in $L^2([0,1])$. Consequently, the Lebesgue probability measure algebra, equipped with the symmetric-difference metric, is an injective uniform space. The construction uses dyadic conditional expectations and a common exponential coupling to obtain Lipschitz maps into the indicator functions that approximate the identity uniformly on that set. As an application, we construct a Polish topological group whose left uniform space is injective but which admits a bounded left uniformly continuous real-valued function that is not right uniformly continuous. This answers the injective part of a question of Bouziad and Troallic in the negative. The group is a semidirect product of two copies of the measure algebra and is also bounded, locally finite, and of exponent at most four.
item.dc:creator: Dekui Peng, Li-Hong Xie, Jiang Yang

item.title: On Separately Continuous Functions of the First Baire Class on Squares and Mixed Products
item.description: arXiv:2611.01818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Mykhaylyuk's problem asking whether the Baire-one property for every separately continuous real-valued function on each of the squares $X^2$ and $Y^2$ implies the same property on $X\times Y$. Assuming $\mathfrak b>\omega_1$, the article obtains a negative answer using the compact cube $K=[-1,1]^{\omega_1}$ and the space $E=(c_{00}(\omega_1),\sigma(c_{00}(\omega_1),\ell_\infty(\omega_1)))$. It presents a finite-coordinate characterization of Baire-one functions on $E$ under this hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Alexander V. Osipov

item.title: Nonpathological submeasures and $F_\sigma$ ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.02266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relationship between nonpathological lower semicontinuous submeasures, $F_\sigma$ ideals on $\omega$, and matrix summability ideals. First, we construct in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ a non-analytic ideal on $\omega$ which is representable as an intersection of matrix summability ideals. Then, we show that an $F_\sigma$ ideal is nonpathological if and only if it can be represented as an intersection of summable ideals if and only if it can be represented as an intersection of matrix summability ideals. We also prove that the random graph ideal is pathological. Finally, we compute the exact degree of pathology of a certain submeasure related to a construction of Tops{\o}e.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Leonetti

item.title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.00363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions. In addition, we associate a special G-pcongruence to each pair of strong G-pmorphisms. Then, we study products, co-products, equalizers, co-equalizers, pullbacks, and pushouts in the category G-pActTop. We find that the category of topological partial actions is finitely complete and contains a co-complete subcategory. Finally, we show that the relationship between a topological partial action and its enveloping action is functorial. As a consequence, we obtain that the categorical product in G-ActTop coincides with the categorical product in G-pActTop. Moreover, the envelope of a co-product in G-pActTop is given by the co-product of the respective envelopes.
item.dc:creator: Jes\'us \'Avila, Fabi\'an Molina

item.title: The ball fixed point property for continuous functions on locally compact spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and $p\in K$. We prove that the Banach space $C(K,p)=\{f\in C(K,\mathbb R):f(p)=0\}$ fails the ball fixed point property (BFPP) whenever $p$ is non-isolated, answering a question of Avil\'es, Jap\'on, Lennard, Mart\'inez-Cervantes and Stawski. Consequently, $C_0(L)$ fails the BFPP for every noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space $L$. Together with Barroso's characterization for $C(K)$, this yields complete topological classifications of the BFPP for $C_0(L)$ and $C(K,p)$. We also resolve a second question of Avil\'es et al., showing that the BFPP of $C(K)$ implies that of $C(K,p)$ for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ and every $P$-point $p\in K$ if and only if there are no measurable cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Lily DiPaulo

item.title: Idempotent Ultrafilters and Closed Images of Complete Semilattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.01545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every continuous homomorphism from a complete topologized semilattice to a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice has closed image, answering a question of Banakh and Bardyla. The main step is the convergence of idempotent ultrafilters on complete semitopological semilattices. We also prove that, for every complete subsemilattice $X$ of a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $Y$, the natural order of $X$ is closed in $Y\times Y$. In particular, the natural order of every complete Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $X$ is closed in $X\times X$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander V. Osipov, Konstantin Kazachenko

item.title: A complete description of the algebraic structure of pseudocompact abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We solve a major open problem from [D. Dikranjan, D. Shakhmatov, Algebraic structure of pseudocompact groups, Memoirs AMS 633 (1998)] by describing abelian groups which admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. First, we prove that an abelian group G can be equipped with a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology iff it can be decomposed into a direct sum G=B\oplus H of a bounded torsion group B and agroup H satisfying |nH|=|H| for all positive integers $n$, such that both B and H admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. Second, for an unbounded abelian group G, we denote by m the minimal positive integer n such that |nG|=|kG| for all integers k\ge n. Then G admits a pseudocompact group topology iff both G[m]={g\in G: mg=0} and mG\cong G/G[m] admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology.
item.dc:creator: Dikran Dikranjan, Alejandro Dorantes-Aldama, Dmitri Shakhmatov

item.title: Circular orders: topology and continuous actions
item.description: arXiv:2512.17314v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the topology of circularly ordered sets. While the algebraic notion is classical, the general topological theory has received comparatively little attention. In this work we provide a self-contained topological exposition and present several new directions and results. Our aim is to initiate a systematic study of generalized circularly ordered topological spaces and of continuous group actions on them. Provide a convex uniform structure description of circularly ordered compactifications. This yields a topological analysis of Novak's regular completion and its uniformity. Demonstrate that this uniform-structure approach yields several new results in the theory of $G$-compactifications for topological group actions on abstract ordered spaces. Reexamine functions of bounded variation on circularly ordered sets and prove generalizations of Helly's selection theorem (for circular and linear orders). These developments and the systematic analysis of circular order topologies are motivated by recent applications in topological dynamics, particularly in joint works with Eli Glasner.
item.dc:creator: Michael Megrelishvili

item.title: Constructions of contractibility in finite subset spaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.09815v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The space of all finite non-empty subsets of a topological space $X$, also known as the Ran space of $X$, is weakly contractible for $X$ path connected. We consider subspaces $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ of the Ran space given by all subsets of $X$ of size at most $n$, and their first homotopy groups. These groups are known to be trivial for $n\geqslant 3$, though the proofs are not constructive. We draw an explicit contraction in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 3}(S^1)$ of the generator of $\pi_1(S^1)$, which we then use to conclude that the induced maps $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to \pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 2n+1}(X))$ and $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to \pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n+2}(X))$ are trivial for all positive integers $n$. Pathological maps with infinitely many strata changes in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ are resolved via locally contractible neighbourhoods and exit paths. From this we conclude the triviality of $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X))$, for all $n\geqslant 3$.
item.dc:creator: J\=anis Lazovskis

item.title: Polish spaces of separable Banach lattices
item.description: arXiv:2607.08064v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compare two Polish presentations of separable real Banach lattices: closed sublattices of a universal lattice and closed ideals of $\operatorname{FBL}[\ell_1]$. We construct translations preserving lattice isometry in both directions, continuous and injective from sublattices to ideals and Borel in the reverse direction. Natural generation and Fremlin tensor operations are $\boldsymbol\Sigma^0_2$-measurable with $G_\delta$ graphs. Isometric lattice isomorphism in either universal coding is Borel bireducible with a complete orbit equivalence relation of Polish-group actions. Uniform monotonicity and order uniform smoothness are $\boldsymbol\Pi^0_3$-complete in both codings, whereas strict monotonicity, order smoothness, and order continuity are coanalytic. Abstract $L_p$ and AM-spaces form closed classes of sublattice codes. We also give explicit Borel bounds for atom counts, compact order intervals, and the lattice-isometry classes of $L_p[0,1]$, $\ell_p$, and $c_0$.
item.dc:creator: Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Pointwise function spaces over compacta are not weak Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.17549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional real Banach space. We prove that there is no continuous bijection $h\colon C_p(K)\to E_w$ whose inverse is continuous at $h(0)$. Consequently, $C_p(K)$ and $C_w(L)$ are not homeomorphic for any infinite compact Hausdorff spaces $K$ and $L$. This settles Krupski's problem and its two-space version due to Krupski and Marciszewski, and answers a question of K\k{a}kol, Leiderman, and Michalak concerning $C_p([0,1])$ and weak Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Jerzy K\k{a}kol

item.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.14074v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $\kappa$-barrelled and $\omega$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $\omega$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $\sigma$-compact, $\omega$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_\kappa$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $\omega$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia V. Ferrer, Salvador Hern\'andez, Isabel Sep\'ulveda
